question: What percentage of health care waste is typically classified as non-hazardous general waste?
explanation: The vast majority of materials discarded in medical facilities are ordinary domestic-type refuse that poses no specialized biological risk. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h1)

question: Why must pathological waste be separated from standard domestic garbage in a clinical setting?

options.A: It is highly recyclable and must be processed by municipal paper recycling plants.
options.B: It decomposes too slowly in standard community landfills and ruins local soil chemistry.
options.C: It consists exclusively of expired liquid medications that dissolve plastic waste bags.
options.D: It contains recognizable body parts that carry infectious agents and require dignified disposal.

explanation: Pathological waste involves tissues and organs that require specialized disposal to prevent disease spread and maintain safety standards. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h1)

question: Which bloodborne pathogen is most commonly transmitted through accidental needle-stick injuries from improperly discarded sharps?
explanation: Hepatitis B has a high viral persistence and infectivity rate, making accidental sharps exposure a primary occupational hazard for health workers. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h2)

question: The open burning of medical plastics directly releases which hazardous air pollutant?
explanation: Burning plastics at low temperatures generates pollutants like dioxins that are harmful to human health and the environment. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h2)

question: Which international organization publishes foundational guidance documents for safe health care waste management?
explanation: The WHO sets global technical standards and publishes reference manuals used by countries to design their national waste policies. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h3)

question: What is the primary function of the Basel Convention regarding global health care refuse?

options.A: It funds the construction of high-temperature incinerators in rural districts.
options.B: It directly penalizes individual nurses who fail to separate sharps.
options.C: It controls the cross-border movement and shipment of hazardous waste.
options.D: It manufactures standardized color-coded bin liners for global distribution.

explanation: This international treaty prevents nations from dumping toxic and medical refuse across borders without strict oversight. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h3)

question: At what point in the clinical workflow must medical waste segregation occur?

options.A: During final loading onto transport lorries
options.D: At the exact point of generation

explanation: Sorting waste immediately where it is produced prevents contamination of general garbage and protects subsequent handlers. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h4)

question: What is the primary design feature required for containers used to collect discarded needles and scalpels?
explanation: Sharps containers must resist penetration from needles to prevent accidental injuries to staff and waste handlers. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h4)

question: Which treatment technology uses high-pressure steam to sterilize infectious medical waste?
explanation: An autoclave subjects infectious materials to high-temperature steam under pressure to destroy microorganisms completely. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h5)

question: Why must sanitary landfills feature engineered bottom liners when accepting treated medical refuse?

options.A: To attract scavenging birds away from residential neighborhoods
options.B: To provide structural support for heavy transport vehicles
options.C: To speed up the natural decomposition of hard plastic syringes
options.D: To prevent toxic liquid leachates from seeping into underground water tables

explanation: Impermeable liners block harmful liquids from migrating into surrounding soil and local community water supplies. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h5)

question: A staff nurse notices that a sharps disposal box is filled past its recommended limit. What action should be taken?

options.A: Wait until the end of the weekly shift before requesting a replacement.
options.B: Seal and replace the box immediately with a new one.
options.C: Transfer some used needles into an ordinary black refuse bag.
options.D: Press down the contents with a gloved hand to create more space.

explanation: Overfilling sharps boxes dramatically increases the risk of needle-stick injuries and must be avoided by sealing them promptly. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h6)

question: How do clinical nurses directly influence safe waste disposal habits among junior nursing students?

options.A: By handling all clinical refuse themselves to shield students from hazards
options.B: By focusing entirely on charting while students manage disposal alone
options.C: By demonstrating proper segregation techniques during routine patient procedures
options.D: By penalizing students financially for every missing plastic bin liner

explanation: Nurses act as clinical role models, shaping safe professional habits through consistent observation and direct supervision. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h6)

question: Which challenge is most frequently encountered when operating advanced waste treatment systems in resource-limited health facilities?

options.A: Excessive surpluses of specialized color-coded bin liners
options.B: An overabundance of trained environmental sanitation inspectors
options.C: Erratic electricity supply and equipment maintenance deficits
options.D: Strict compliance with international export shipping bans

explanation: Unreliable power grids and a lack of spare parts often render heavy machinery like autoclaves and incinerators inoperable. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h7)

question: What is an effective strategy for improving waste segregation in facilities with severe financial constraints?

options.A: Importing expensive automated robotic sorting stations from abroad
options.B: Implementing continuous staff education and low-cost visual sorting charts
options.C: Mixing all hospital refuse together to save money on multiple bins
options.D: Stopping all invasive medical procedures until new incinerators arrive

explanation: Practical training and clear local signage improve staff compliance without requiring expensive high-tech infrastructure. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h7)
